title: Aṅga-vandana: the twelve names

words.role: said while touching the right cheek
said while touching the left cheek

words.meaning: Mādhava, ‘descendant of Madhu’ or ‘husband of Mā (Lakṣmī)’
words.role: said while touching the right eye
said while touching the left eye
said while touching the right nostril
said while touching the left nostril
said while touching the right ear
said while touching the left ear
said while touching the right shoulder
said while touching the left shoulder

words.meaning: Dāmodara, ‘with a cord round the waist’

translation.literal: O Keśava, O Nārāyaṇa, O Mādhava, O Govinda, O Viṣṇu, O Madhusūdana, O Trivikrama, O Vāmana, O Śrīdhara, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O Padmanābha, O Dāmodara.
translation.readable: Keśava, Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava, Govinda, Viṣṇu, Madhusūdana, Trivikrama, Vāmana, Śrīdhara, Hṛṣīkeśa, Padmanābha, Dāmodara.

meaning: The twelve names of Viṣṇu, called in the vocative, one for each part of the face and body touched after the sipping: the two cheeks, the eyes, the nostrils, the ears, the shoulders, the navel and the head. The same twelve names receive water at the tarpaṇa later in the rite (tarpana-kesava), there in the accusative.
in_the_rite: Ācamana (step acamana), after the three sips: each name is said while touching one place — the stotrasamhita text gives the order cheeks, eyes, nostrils, ears, shoulders, navel, head, with the finger for each.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: All twelve are vocatives; viṣṇo is the vocative of viṣṇu, the others of a-stems, which have no ending in the vocative.
